description: Experiment J: matched TG/RFC × lens × structural views, on the documented synthetic 13-node hybrid input.

definitions.protection: Both TG and RFC controls preserve the nominated focal members using production source-neighborhood projection. Only the RFC force callback differs. Explicit filters still override protection; this isolates force from view membership.
definitions.matching: Each reduced view is paired with the full control at the same seed/focus/force/lens. Both are scored on the reduced view's retained radial IDs, branch sets, visible node pairs and semantic edges. Hidden coordinates never enter these scores.
definitions.angular: Angular RMS uses 2pi/N for each retained branch set. These are common-subset scores, not the full graph's original angular objective when degrees differ. Each recorded inventory preserves nominal and retained branch sets.
definitions.radial: Distance minus the explicit RFC target 120, isotropic coordinates. The ordinary TG edge length parameter 90 is an attraction denominator, not a rest-length target.
definitions.display: HyperLens 0 or 60 about the moving Project A center, unit graph/canvas scale, zero pan/rotation. Physical integrations must be identical across lens twins. Point pairs below 30 and proper straight-segment intersections are proxies, not label/body/routed-edge readability.
definitions.motion: Every actual integration is sampled, including the tenth in every batch. Trace points show batch 1/every tenth/final batch; their motion covers that batch, not the skipped interval. Large means >29.9 Euclidean units; clipped means at least one axis reaches 30.
definitions.force: Post-run net impulse RMS on visible nodes, with retained momentum cleared and global movement stopped; divide by rigidity. Probe cannot move saved coordinates and is excluded from motion totals.
definitions.scope: One small synthetic semantic graph, two focal choices, five jittered starts, four view rules. No figure reproduction, general convergence, human readability or large-graph claim.
